{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's own brief undercuts it. The exact feature already ships in at least five live products. Several bundle it free or at $1-4/mo (ProxiedMail includes alias replies on its free tier), and a free open-source Thunderbird extension already solves the client-side case. The brief gives no evidence that anyone would pay for a standalone version.",
    "Idea B has much stronger, sourced willingness-to-pay evidence. Six competitors charge $67-$799 for the US side. Reddit users report accountant quotes of $800-$2,500. So one sale at $150-$300 is plausible on price alone.",
    "Idea B cites a sourced precedent that a single founder (Atamatax) built and sells a narrow, PFIC-aware self-serve tool at $199-$799+. That is direct evidence the one-person model can work in this market. Idea A has no comparable evidence of a standalone product earning money.",
    "Idea B also has a sourced, unsolved differentiator: Atamatax's own site calls local-country filing 'the hard part.' Idea A's brief identifies no whitespace that incumbents leave open.",
    "Idea B's risks are real but can be narrowed. The brief's open questions point toward a single country pairing as the wedge. Idea A's core problem, a commodity priced near zero, cannot be scoped away."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand quotes come from generic Zoho, Apple Mail and Outlook users who want replies sent from a business alias (e.g. info@ vs. admin@). They are mail-client configuration complaints, not evidence from the stated payer (privacy-conscious prosumers juggling many aliases). None of the quotes shows willingness to pay. The Reddit CPC figure is also a generic platform average, not specific to privacy subreddits.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. B wins mainly because A's brief documents that its product is already free or bundled. B carries serious feasibility risks within 90 days. The brief gives no timeline for the IRS EFIN application or software acceptance testing. Per-country tax liability is unresolved. The Meta CPL figure is a cross-industry average that the brief says likely understates this niche. Seasonal filing timing is not addressed. If B's MVP collapses to US-only filing, it enters a crowded market, and the margin of preference narrows considerably."
}
